title: Onramp: Embeddings Mini-Sprint Lab Notes (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures lab-run notes for a short, focused onramp sprint that helps developers integrate embeddings into a sample product flow using the Redwood SDK. The goal is to produce a tiny, repeatable kit (demo app + troubleshooting checklist + telemetry hooks) that can be used by SDK advocates and SEs in customer pilots.

Target audience:
- Software engineers evaluating embeddings for search, similarity, and reranking.
- Solutions engineers running 30–90 minute customer workshops.
- Developer advocates preparing a reproducible demo.

Desired outcomes (MVP by end of sprint):
1) Starter repo skeleton that:
   - calls the Redwood embeddings API via SDK (JS + Python examples)
   - persists vectors in a lightweight store (SQLite + incl. schema)
   - implements a minimal similarity search endpoint with fallback model
2) Short quickstart guide (5–7 steps, copyable commands) and one-pager cheat sheet.
3) Telemetry recipe: minimal events to capture (latency, token usage, embed-dim mismatch, index size).
4) Troubleshooting checklist for common failure modes.

Sprint agenda (60–120m workshop template):
- 00:00–00:10 Intro + why embeddings matter (use cases: search, classification, rerank)
- 00:10–00:30 Live coding: generate embeddings for a small corpus (JS example)
- 00:30–00:45 Persist + query: nearest neighbour search, naive similarity scoring
- 00:45–00:55 Ops + telemetry: show latency/usage in Console + describe cost levers
- 00:55–01:00 Wrap up + ask for feedback (micro-survey link)

Quickstart (5 steps) — copy/paste friendly:
1) Install SDK: npm i @redwood/inference  OR pip install redwood-sdk
2) Set REDWOOD_API_KEY and region env var
3) Create embeddings for corpus:
   JS: 
   const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
   const resp = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'embed-lite-1', input: ['doc1 text', 'doc2 text'] });
   // persist resp.data -> sqlite table `vectors` (id, vector, text, meta)
4) Query: compute query embedding, cosine-sim top-k, return results
5) Inspect telemetry: console.redwood.io -> project -> embeddings -> token/latency breakdown

Sample minimal SQLite schema (for demo):
- vectors(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, text TEXT, embedding BLOB, metadata JSON, created_at TEXT)
- indexes: created_at, metadata->'source'

JS pseudocode for similarity (naive):
- compute query embedding from API
- for each row in vectors: score = dot(query, candidate) / (||q|| * ||c||)
- return top-k sorted by score

Telemetry & acceptance metrics (what to capture in the SDK demo):
- event: embedding.request (fields: model, token_count, corpus_size, duration_ms, status)
- event: embed.indexing (count_inserted, latency_ms)
- alerting thresholds: p95 latency > 300ms for embed.create, daily token spike > 2x baseline
- customer-facing KPI: median query latency (end-to-end) < 120ms for 1k corpus in demo environment

Failure modes observed in practice (and mitigations):
1) Mismatch embed dimensions (user supplied previous embeddings): detect dim != model.dim and return clear error: "embedding dimension mismatch (expected 1536) — see migration notes".
2) Cost surprises on large batches: default to small batch sizes (16) and show cost estimate before bulk ops. Add a confirm prompt for >500 items.
3) Slow queries due to inefficient scan: demo defaults to SQLite linear scan for small corpora (<5k). Add note: switch to FAISS/Annoy for >5k items and link to migration guide.
4) Tokenization gotchas: warn users about truncation for multi-part documents; provide a function snippet to chunk and dedupe.

Developer ergonomics notes (things to include in the quick kit):
- Prebuilt chunker: python/js utility chunk_text(text, max_chars=4000, overlap=100)
- Vector serializer helpers: base64 vs binary; recommend base64 JSON-safe for Drive demos
- Small helper to compute cosine in JS: fast typed-array routine
- Local dev mode: stubbed SDK that returns deterministic vectors for fast offline demos (see tests/stubbed-client.js)

Debug checklist for SEs (one-liner items):
- [ ] API key valid and scoped to embeddings
- [ ] Model name correct and supported in region
- [ ] No dimension mismatch after embedding creation
- [ ] DB writes succeed (check sqlite file perms)
- [ ] Query returns >0 results for known keyword queries
- [ ] Console shows embedding.request events after run

Open questions (need product/infra input):
- Default model choice for starter kit: embed-lite-1 vs embed-accurate-2? tradeoffs: dim, cost, latency. (Elena to sync with model team)
- Should we include a small in-repo FAISS binary or point to hosted FAISS? (SRE / infra preference)
- Rate limit guidance for parallel indexing — what burst policy do Dedicated/private customers get? (ask infra)

Customer anecdotes & contextual notes (for talk track):
- Retail search pilot: vector size + chunking decision drove relevance improvement from 42% -> 78% for long product descriptions.
- Legal docs: chunk overlap and metadata (doc id / paragraph id) crucial to avoid hallucination during retrieval-augmented generation.

Next steps (owners + ETA):
- [Morgan] Draft quickstart guide + repo skeleton (ETA: 2025-10-10)
- [Elena] Confirm model recommendation and doc snippet (ETA: 2025-10-08)
- [Kai] Create a stubbed SDK mode for offline demos and add tests (ETA: 2025-10-12)
- [Samir] Wire telemetry events into demo, create Console dashboard template (ETA: 2025-10-15)

Meeting notes (live scribe):
- Client-side: recommend serde into JSON-base64 embedding to avoid sqlite BLOB pitfalls.
- Pricing concern: show quick calculator in quickstart to estimate token cost for indexing.
- Docs tone: keep the main quickstart under 300 words, move deeper ops details to an advanced.md.

Quick links / references to include in final kit:
- Confluence: Embeddings design spec (internal link)
- GH: example app PR once ready (PR link placeholder)
- Jira: onboarding ticket template (DE-789)

Notes to self: keep this doc small and action-oriented. The Drive doc is the working area; once the skeleton repo and guide are stable we'll publish a polished copy to Confluence and create a short slide deck for SEs.

Unresolved items for next sync: model default, faiss vs hosted index, small-section on privacy/KMS for Private deployments.
